summary: Inspected all four supplied PNGs at native 1x and nearest 3x. The large vermilion/gold silhouette reads as a phoenix: hooked beak, forked crest, broad folded wings, three separated tail ends and two bronze feet. Upper-left highlights and broad red shadow clusters give the wings and neck volume; the far folded wing is somewhat plate-like but remains legible. Neck, wing roots and legs appear connected. The transparent space between the standing legs is intentional; no obvious accidental interior pinholes or detached anatomy were visible across the light, dark and checker previews. Bronze toes have modest contrast on the dark background, but the planted stance remains readable. Idle frames preserve the ground contact while changing small neck/feather clusters. Windup folds the neck, move opens the near wing and steps, attack extends a connected forward claw with the other foot supporting the body, recover folds back, hit recoils through the neck, and dead lies low with the head and folded wing still identifiable. The nine additional frames read as distinct authored states: skill_a places a gold-white core under the wing, skill_b opens the beak into a connected two-branch red/gold flame, and skill_c folds the wing with three separated embers. Poison droops the neck with purple bubbles; stun droops farther with gold stars; sleep crouches with a lowered head and closed eye. Their paired changes are subtle at 1x, but visible in neck/wing clusters as well as effect positions, rather than whole-body tints. No hand or tool applies to this creature. This is a visual keep recommendation, not a user selection. Static pose previews cannot establish playback timing, dash/contact behavior against a target, actual battle-scale readability, or literal pxgrid authorship/model provenance. Geometry alone was not treated as visual approval.
